_why: Not every markdown file in these repos is a documentation page, and the rules
that describe a page's SHAPE were firing on files whose shape something else
already owns.
Measured on 2026-09-07 across studio-docs: 3,789 tier-1 findings, of which
2,558 were on files that are never published. 254 of those were FM-01 asking
for SEO front matter on an agent skill file, and 366 were C1-01 asking for an
Overview and a Next Steps section on the same files. docs/sync-plan.json lists
170 published pages. Nothing under docs/prompts/ or skills/ is among them.
docs/prompts/ and skills/src/ are byte-identical mirrors of one another, so
every finding there is also counted twice. studio-docs/scripts/lint-skills.ts
owns their shape: name-only front matter, a `## When to use` body section, a
token budget, and mirror parity. Asking them for `seo_title` contradicts that
linter rather than adding a check nobody was doing.
This is a scoping statement, not a suppression list. Every PROSE rule still
applies everywhere: casual language, marketing phrasing, buzzwords,
anthropomorphism, emoji, italics, typographic substitutes. A skill file is
read by a model and by the humans who maintain it, and both are better served
by house prose. Only the rules that assert 'a published documentation page
looks like this' are scoped, and each one is listed by id below so that
widening the exemption takes an edit here rather than a quiet default.
Order matters: the first pattern whose prefix matches wins, so put the most
specific path first.

published.what: A page that ships to the docs site. docs/sync-plan.json is the authority on which ones those are. Every rule applies.

agent-prompt.what: A skill or prompt file read by an agent, not by a reader on the docs site. studio-docs/scripts/lint-skills.ts owns its front matter, its section shape and its mirror parity.

internal.what: Working notes, research and contributor guidance that live in the repo and never publish. No SEO front matter, and no obligation to the section matrix.
